newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland allows retail diesel to rise 15-25 percent.
newsitem.headline: Poland allows retail diesel to rise 15-25 percent.

text.p: Polish diesel oil prices have risen 15 to 25 percent over the past few weeks as retailers sold material bought from state reserves at above official price ceilings set for domestically-produced fuels, an industry official said on Thursday.

"The average price of diesel at petrol stations has risen by between 0.2 to 0.3 zlotys per liter," Andrzej Szczesniak, the president of the liquid fuels chamber (PIPP) grouping private fuel retailers and importers, told Reuters.
He said retailers were taking advantage of finance ministry's decision to allow sales of fuels bought at auctions of state reserves at higher prices than the official caps.

Earlier the industry ministry tried to persuade fuel distributors that the official cap at 1.22 zlotys per litre applied to all retailers, even those who bought fuel from the state reserves at higher prices.
Anna Sobocinska from the finance ministry's press department said that the only restriction imposed on retailers selling diesel from the reserves concerned the amount of retail margening.
"The diesel from state reserves can be sold at the purchase price increased by a distribution margin which should not exceed 213 zlotys per tonne," she said.

Last month the goverment decided to unlock state reserves of diesel to avoid market shortages in a period of increased demand, especially from farmers, which coincided with a steep rise in world oil prices.

The government has been selling diesel reserves at weekly auctions. Prices at the last auction on October 2, when the industry ministry offered 100,000 tonnes of fuel prices ranged between 1.19 and 1.41 zlotys per litre.
